title: Speed a stretch up, slow a moment down
goal: Long recordings have dead stretches and moments worth dwelling on. Let a piece be sped up or slowed down, so a two minute wait becomes four seconds and the click worth seeing gets half a second to land.
notes:
Build on docs/design/mocks/pages/video-speed.html: "Retiming is a property of the selected clip, so nothing new appears in the chrome. The clip sits on the timeline dock, its speed curve is plotted on the clip's own time axis right below it."

So no retime mode and no separate window. A speed curve under the clip is the page's answer and is a good one.

The audio question is the one people get wrong. Speeding up video and leaving the audio chipmunked is a bug; dropping the audio silently is worse. Decide, and say it where somebody will read it.

---
Grounded in the video clickthroughs, which the user says are ideas to build on rather than specs: say in the audit where you went further or differently and why. The thesis every page shares governs this too: video is not a mode, it is the layer document with time.
acceptance: A clip can be given a speed, and the timeline shows it taking less or more room as a result
Speed can change across a clip rather than only being one number for the whole thing
What happens to the audio is deliberate and stated: say whether it changes pitch, is corrected, or is dropped, and why
A sped up stretch still plays smoothly rather than stuttering, and the audit says what it did about frames
Everything downstream moves correctly when a clip changes length, following the same ripple rule cutting uses
What plays is what exports, timed rather than eyeballed
Audit under queue/audits/ with a real capture retimed, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. What already exists: ClipPiece.speedPercent, atSpeed, setClipSpeed, the within-clip ripple (pieces are laid back to back so a retime pushes the rest along by construction), Video > Speed with 25/50/100/200/400, and a varispeed on playback. What is missing is everything that makes it a feature a person can find and trust: (1) nothing in the Properties panel, which is exactly where the mock puts it ('retiming is a property of the selected clip, so nothing new appears in the chrome'); (2) the audio answer is a code comment and nothing a user ever reads; (3) the goal's own example - a two minute wait becomes four seconds - is 30x, and the model caps at 10x, so the task cannot meet its own goal as built; (4) nothing anywhere says what retiming does about frames.

left rough (no task, written here): (1) the mock's speed CURVE with draggable stops and a ramp between them is deliberately not built - speed varies across a clip by the clip being in pieces, which is the model cutting and reordering already use, and a smooth ramp is a cinematic flourish where these recordings are screens. It is an idea to react to in the audit, not a defect. (2) At 30x a two second piece becomes 67ms, two frames, which is very hard to grab again on the timeline. That is the honest consequence of the speed rather than a bug, and undo is easier than grabbing it. Neither clears the follow-up bar; the panel-order crowding did and was folded into appearance-is-below-the-fold-again-because-the-p.

A Speed section in the Properties panel retimes the clip or the piece in hand (Sources/Photonz/SpeedInspector.swift) over a new pure model in PhotonzCore/ClipSpeed.swift: the stops (25 to 3000 per cent), what the sound does at each of them, and what the retime did to the length and to the frames. Ceiling raised 10x -> 30x so the task's own goal (a two minute wait becomes four seconds) is reachable. The audio decision is made and stated: it goes with the picture between half speed and double and is SILENT outside that band, said in the panel in a sentence rather than dropped quietly, with ClipPiece.playsSound the one gate the player, exporter and waveform all read. Verified: 8740 tests green including 16 new; speed-a-stretch-walk drives the panel with real presses, takes 9 real window captures, and reads the exported files back (8s at 4x -> a 2.0s file, silent; at 2x -> 4.0s, with sound). Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-21-video-speed.json. Committed 70b781f1.
